newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Heshe to spin off Hong Kong unit.
newsitem.headline: Heshe to spin off Hong Kong unit.

text.p: Garment manufacturer and retailer Heshe Holdings Ltd plans to list its subsidiary, Benefun International Holdings Ltd, on the Hong Kong and the Singapore stock exchange, Heshe said in a statement on Wednesday.
Heshe said Benefun has sent in applications for a primary listing on the Hong Kong exchange as well as a secondary listing on the Singapore exchange
Benefun makes, distributes and retails branded casual wear in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong.
For the financial year ended June 30 1996, the Benefun group achieved a turnover of HK$544.2 million and made a net profit of HK$38.8 million.
Heshe said the listing will allow Benefun to raise fresh funds for expansion.
In relation to the listing, Benefun proposes to offer 100 million new shares representing 25 percent of its enlarged share capital to investors in Hong Kong.
At the same time, Heshe plans to sell its entire stake in Benefun comprising 236.52 million shares in a preferential sale to Heshe shareholders.
The sale, to be handed by DBS Bank, will be on the basis of a mininum of 680 to a maximum of 758 Benefun shares for every 1,000 Heshe shares.

The price of the preferential shares will be offered at a fixed price based on the Singapore dollar equivalent of the initial public offer of the new shares in Hong Kong. The offer price will be determined at a later date.

Heshe said the sale of Benefun will help it finance its move to seek new core businesses. The sale would also result in an extraordinary gain of not less than S$5.7 million for the current financial year ending June 30 1997.
